title: EXPC-GVP Vocabulary Entity
$comment: x-schema-version is EXPC-GVP-specific metadata, not a JSON Schema keyword. See docs/01_DATA_SCHEMA.md for the versioning model (schema version vs Builder SemVer vs Data Pack CalVer) and for design decisions referenced below. 0.2.0 (Phase 01.1) is a backward-compatible additive change: it adds an optional structured alias form ($defs/alias_entry) alongside the existing plain-string form. Every document valid under 0.1.0 remains valid under 0.2.0 unchanged -- see docs/01_DATA_SCHEMA.md 'Per-alias policy model' for why this is a MINOR bump, not a MAJOR one.
description: Contract for a single EXPC Global Vocabulary Pack entity. One JSON document (or one array element, depending on how a data pack chooses to store entities) must validate against this schema per vocabulary entity.

id.description: Stable machine identifier, conventionally '<kind>.<slug>' (e.g. 'brand.microsoft'). Once published, an id must never be reused for a different entity. Consistency between the id prefix and the 'kind' field is a repository convention enforced by tests/, not by this schema (kind values may gain dashes/segments over time that would complicate a single regex).

kind.description: Semantic category of the entity. Deliberately a closed, small enum aligned 1:1 with the data/ subdirectory taxonomy established in Phase 00.1 (brands, software, ai, hardware, standards, networking). NOT the same axis as 'layer' -- a company (kind=brand) can still be public/Global (layer=global).

layer.description: Vocabulary layer per docs/02_VOCABULARY_LAYERS.md. The public EXPC-GVP repository's data/ directory must only ever contain layer='global' or layer='domain' entries. 'organization' and 'personal' are valid schema values (the same schema may be reused by private, non-public vocabulary stores) but must never appear as real entities in this public repository.

language.description: ISO 639-1 language/script code of the 'canonical' spelling itself (e.g. 'en' for 'Microsoft'), not the nationality of the entity behind it.

canonical.description: The canonical original spelling. Always preferred by default ('prefer canonical original'). Must not be a translation and must not be a transcription -- see docs/01_DATA_SCHEMA.md.

aliases.description: Alternate spoken/written forms, keyed by ISO 639-1 language code (the language of the alias forms themselves, not necessarily the entity's own 'language' -- e.g. entity language 'en' can still have Russian aliases under aliases.ru). May be an empty object ({}) if no aliases are known yet -- the key must still be present (fail-safe explicitness, see provenance below for the same principle). Aliases are informal/variant forms; they are not translations (see 'ru_equivalent') and not the preferred phonetic rendering (see 'ru_transcription'). Each entry is either a plain string (legacy/simple form, schema 0.1.0-compatible) or a structured object with optional per-alias policy overrides -- see $defs/alias_entry and docs/01_DATA_SCHEMA.md 'Per-alias policy model'. uniqueItems only catches exact literal duplicates (same representation); normalization-aware duplicate detection across string/object representations of the same alias text is Builder's job (tools/builder/validator.py), not the schema's.

ru_equivalent.description: An actual Russian-language semantic equivalent/translation of the canonical term, when one genuinely exists and is distinct from a phonetic rendering (e.g. canonical 'mouse' -> ru_equivalent 'мышь'). null means no established Russian equivalent exists -- this is the expected, common value for untranslated proper nouns/brand names, not a placeholder for missing data.

ru_transcription.description: The preferred phonetic Cyrillic rendering of 'canonical' (e.g. 'Майкрософт' for 'Microsoft'). This is distinct from 'aliases.ru', which may contain multiple informal/variant spoken forms in addition to (or instead of) this preferred rendering. null means no transcription has been curated yet.

policy.description: Replacement-strategy classification -- see docs/03_COLLISION_POLICY.md. This enum may gain values in a future minor schema version; a consumer that encounters an unrecognized policy value MUST fail safe and treat it as 'context_required'.

auto_replace.description: Whether a consumer may safely replace a matched alias with 'canonical' without additional context/boundary checks. See the cross-field constraints below: high ambiguity and policy=context_required both force this to false.

source.description: 'official' = obtained directly from a reviewed, authoritative source per SOURCES.md. 'curated' = authored/compiled by an EXPC-GVP contributor from general knowledge, not yet run through the SOURCES.md review process. 'community' = contributed by a third party. 'unverified' = explicitly not checked.

source_url.description: URL of the reviewed source, or null if none has been recorded yet. Pattern is a loose sanity check, not a strict URI format validation (no extra format-validation dependency is used at this phase).

confidence.description: Curator confidence in the correctness/currency of this entity, 0-1. Not a substitute for provenance.source -- a high confidence value does not imply the entity has been through formal source review.

last_verified.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) this entity's provenance fields were last confirmed, or null if never formally verified against SOURCES.md.

alias_entry.description: One entry in an aliases['<lang>'] array. Either a plain string (legacy/simple form -- fully inherits ambiguity/policy/auto_replace from the entity) or a structured object carrying optional per-alias overrides of those same three fields. See docs/01_DATA_SCHEMA.md 'Per-alias policy model' for the entity-default -> alias-override inheritance rule and docs/03_COLLISION_POLICY.md for worked examples (Wi-Fi, CUDA).

value.description: The alias text itself -- equivalent to what a plain-string entry would be.

ambiguity.description: Overrides the entity's 'ambiguity' for this alias only. Absent = inherit the entity's value.

policy.description: Overrides the entity's 'policy' for this alias only. Absent = inherit the entity's value.

auto_replace.description: Overrides the entity's 'auto_replace' for this alias only. Absent = inherit the entity's value.

oneOf.$comment: This allOf only catches a LOCALLY self-contradictory alias object: if THIS alias object states ambiguity=high or policy=context_required, it must ALSO state auto_replace=false on itself. It cannot see the entity's own ambiguity/policy/auto_replace, so it cannot catch an unsafe EFFECTIVE combination produced by merging a partial override with entity defaults -- e.g. an alias that overrides ONLY auto_replace=true while ambiguity/policy are left to inherit an unsafe entity-level ambiguity=high or policy=context_required. That cross-cutting, entity+alias merge check is Builder's job (tools/builder/validator.py + tools/builder/policy.py), not the schema's -- consistent with this schema's existing structural-contract-only role.
